utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I would ask the Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-01-48-PT, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Vladimir Tochilovsky, that's me; Marie Tuma to my right; and Manoj Sachdeva to her right. And Hasan Younis, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, my name is Stefan Kirsch, and together with me is Guenael Mettraux, also counsel for Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The position today as far as this case is concerned is this -- that it seems almost certain that another case is to be listed starting very shortly, which will go on beyond the 19th of January, the date from which it had been declared, this case would start trial. Effectively it means that this case will not, therefore, commence on the 19th of January, unless there is a very unlikely development within this week, which is, as I say, seems unlikely. We therefore propose to deal with this particular matter as a Status Conference. I'm not in a position, I'm afraid, to give a date for this trial to start now. It is a matter beyond the competence, beyond the control of the Trial Chamber. We will make sure that those who do have responsibility for listing recognise the length of time which has passed since this accused made his initial appearance. It is, of course, a case in which the accused is on provisional release, and therefore it's not a case in which there is that concern. But nonetheless, it is a case which plainly should be tried, it is not in the public interest, that even if an accused person is on provisional release that his case does not -- be heard. As I say, there is no -- at the moment no date which I can give you, but it is a matter which we will be bringing to the attention of those who have responsibility for listing the cases and to make sure that the date is found for it and a Trial Chamber as soon as possible. That said, we propose to go through the various outstanding matters and deal with them. The disclosure and the like. We will give such rulings as we can and deal with any matters that we can. And then I'll hear from both sides whether there are any matters they wish to raise. We have helpfully been provided by the Senior Legal Officer with a list of potentially outstanding matters. There are a number of motions which it may be convenient to deal with as we go through. There is a Prosecution motion applying for an order for nondisclosure filed on the 11th of December. In fact, the materials, as I understand it, have already been disclosed. But it may be that time is not yet up for the Defence to respond, but it may be that they can give a voluntary undertaking. The motion was only filed last week. They may not have had a chance to consider it. But it may be that the sensible way to deal with it is an undertaking by the Defence not to disclose the material, except to the extent necessary for the preparation of the Defence. Mr. Kirsch, are you in a position to give that undertaking at the moment or would you rather bide your time and respond as soon as you can?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to apologise, I have not spoken thoroughly about the matter with Mr. Mettraux. Maybe he's in a position to give you some thoughts about the Defence. So maybe it's a better idea to respond within the time limit given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would, with having in mind the possibility of giving a voluntary undertaking, which would save time. I have no doubt that that can be done. Mr. Mettraux, no doubt you could have a look at that. Very well. I understand that matters of disclosure have all been completed, both Rule 66 and Rule 68. Perhaps the Prosecution could confirm that for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Yes. With some additional disclosure, which is prepared for giving to the Defence today, right now, all this disclosure 66(A) and 66(B) has been completed. As to the 66(B), the files are accessible for the Defence at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. The next matter we turn to is a matter related to expert reports, which Judge Kwon is to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just to let you know for the record, the Defence will be entitled to cross-examine the expert witness, since the Prosecution is not opposed to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The issue of reciprocal disclosure I turn to next. This has been a case which, from a very early stage, has been made much more difficult by the changes of the Defence. This has no bearing, I should say, on the current Defence team who have stepped into the breach. But I'm sorry to say that the previous Defence counsel have at the very best let the case down. And it has been a matter of great regret that things haven't gotten further advanced so that it could be heard. I would add that the reason this case hasn't been heard before is very much due to the failure, partly on behalf of Defence counsel, partly on problems which have arisen in the Defence that this matter has not been dealt with earlier. But is there any question of matters of reciprocal disclosure, Mr. Kirsch or Mr. Mettraux? Perhaps you could deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you are certainly aware, I was assigned to this case on the 3rd of November, and I didn't have a chance to review all the material that was collected by the Defence team and the investigators before. So it was my position that before the Defence has not made up his mind as to which materials we intend to use either during the Prosecution case or the Defence case, it would have been my ethical obligation to have a look at it first. And we agreed with the Prosecution, we are going to Sarajevo tomorrow. I hope that at the end of the week I will have a rough idea of what is in this material, what is in those documents. And as soon as we make the decision that we are going to -- we are intending to use the material at trial, certainly the Prosecution will have a chance or will get the chance to look at those materials. If they need copies, we will provide them with copies. So I think we reached that agreement and I hope there shouldn't be any problem. The problem arose because of the fact that -- I was not aware when we had the first meeting, the first 65 ter conference that former counsel has cross-referenced a lot of material in the Defence pre-trial brief. My understanding is this is not going to show that the Defence at this point of time was intending to use that material; however, if the Trial Chamber could give us some guidance on that, we would be ready to file a motion to clarify on that matter. But certainly, as I understood Mr. Tochilovsky, the Prosecution and the Defence could live with a practical agreement for the next weeks. And I think within the next week we will resolve it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. While you're on your feet, Mr. Kirsch, perhaps you could deal with another matter which concerns the agreed facts. And I understand that the position is that the copy of the agreed facts which was in fact signed by the accused himself is a subject of a motion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: We filed a motion. I'm not exactly sure at which date -- Mr. Mettraux is looking at the date. And with the Court's indulgence maybe I can ask Mr. Mettraux to clarify on that, that he was the one who drafted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, I'm not sure that I would regard as very satisfactory any notion that there could be a going back on what had been agreed. Mr. Mettraux, perhaps you could assist us on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honours. We have indeed filed a Defence motion regarding the agreed facts on the 11th of December. And as you pointed out, this agreement was indeed signed by Mr. Halilovic and by Mr. Balijagic who was counsel at the time. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What are you proposing to do, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think we had a rather pragmatic approach to this issue. The Defence is concerned by a number of facts to which counsel at the time and the accused might have seemed to agree. And we believe that if this agreement was set aside, we could very quickly be given an opportunity either to explain the extent of the agreement or respond to perhaps a new list of stipulations by the Prosecution. This was our approach. As we understand from our client that he did not receive adequate explanation as to the scope and the meaning of many of the facts to which he agreed, or at least appeared to agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That motion is before the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since this matter is brought in open court. And the time to respond hasn't expired yet, but if we could hear the Prosecution's position right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have agreed facts. And as it was mentioned by the Presiding Judge, it was signed not only, it appears, by Defence counsel, but also by the accused, and we considered this document as agreed facts. We also understand that during the trial that the Defence filed reasons to challenge any of the agreed facts. They are not prohibited by that. So I see no reason, again, to go back and consider the whole procedure on agreed facts. Again, I would just like to emphasise to the Defence, if they have during the trial any challenges to any specific agreed facts, it's always open for that. This is our understanding. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you will put your saying into writing later?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Yes, will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The outstanding motion -- an outstanding motion which in a sense the fact that the trial is no longer taking place as soon as anticipated may be more capable of resolution. And I have in mind the 92 bis motion for some 41 witnesses. The Prosecution, do you -- the Defence, I should say, are due to respond to that next week, 22nd of December. Are you in a position to do that, Mr. Kirsch, or would you ask for many time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask for more time, given the fact that we are travelling to Sarajevo, as I stated before, at the end of the week. And my understanding is that this 92 bis motion is crucial at the beginning of the trial. It would be much more easier for us to agree not to cross-examine a witness after we heard some of the evidence, but I understand that we should deal with that matter before the start of the trial. And so, to give you as much help as we can, I would really like to have a longer deadline to respond. I fear that we have to -- if we have to respond by next Monday, we are not in a position to look at thoroughly as we should into the material. And rather, our position would be then more strict to save our position saying we would need to cross-examine. And then maybe we would come back to you and say, well, we reconsidered our position. But to be as helpful as possible, I think this is crucial that we have enough time to go through every witness statement. And I don't really know what the time frame for this case will be, so I don't know if I would ask for too much, but if we could do it by the mid of January. I think this would be my proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think time is not the pressure it was. It's much more important that you deal with the matter adequately. It is now the practice, whatever one may think of it, it is the practice that we try and do this before the trial rather than waiting for the trial to start. If I may say speaking for myself -- because I'm of a sense in what you say, which is to see what the witnesses say and enable us to start with and then decide which witnesses you need or not. But in any event this is done pre-trial. Now this is of course more difficult for everybody and the danger is that Defence again ask for many more witnesses than they may, in fact, need. So perhaps you might like to think how long you need. Perhaps you have talked with Mr. Mettraux about it to deal with 40 witnesses and, of course, you've got to take instructions from your client as to what he can say about these matters. If you would like to have a word with Mr. Mettraux now and think how long you would need to get a full answer, full and considered answer in, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you. We just discussed it a little bit. Given the fact that we have this Christmas week and then the new year, and it is our understanding that we would be prepared in the second week of January. I mean, the more time we get, the better it is. If you want to hear a day, let's say the 19th of January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What we will do to make sure there's no misunderstanding, we'll give you to the end of January, which will give you a complete month to work on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And to give as full a response as possible. Of course, we would encourage you if you feel able to admit the witnesses, if you feel you properly can, of course that is done as much as possible. But there's no pressure, of course, to do it. You must do whatever's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, we will receive the response. If necessary, we will have a hearing, but otherwise we will give a ruling on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there anything the parties want to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Just one small point. It is the list of issues for previous conference we had on 65 ter with the Senior Legal Officer, and it's about the length of trial. How cross-examination of our 92 bis witnesses will affect the length estimation of that. And our estimation is if we are considered to have twenty-one 92 bis witnesses to be cross-examined, it will take - again it's our estimation - approximately one week or five working days, plus to those four or four and a half months of trial. Thank you. We have no other issues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence, are there any matters you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Nothing in particular, Your Honour. Just to give you notice that we filed a motion this afternoon in relation to the conditions of accommodation of Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll consider that when we get it in. Well, the position then as I said at the outset is that unless there's some very unforeseen circumstances, this case will not come on the 19th of January. It will find a date as early as possible. Meanwhile, we will have to fix a date for the next conference, which will be in the week -- if we could find a convenient date in the week before Easter. If my recollection is right, Easter is -- Good Friday is the 8th of April. We need to find a date in the week before that. So a word with the Senior Legal Officer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The actual date will be known to the parties in due course. And one thing I'd like to clarify is that in the decision of 14th of November this year, the Trial Chamber ordered the Prosecution to identify those witnesses who have entered into favourable arrangements, if any. I don't remember I have received any. But was the communication done between the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We disclosed not only names of those two witnesses but also provided the Defence with the documents related to those arrangements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That's all we can deal with today. We'll adjourn until the next hearing, of which we will notify you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: at 3.29 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Trial Chamber and Senior Legal Officer confer]
